ORDER % 08.08.2025 1. Exemption allowed subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

3. By way of the present petition, the petitioner seeks quashing of the FIR no. 180/2023 dated 19.07.2023, registered at Police Station Sector-23, Dwarka for the offences punishable under Sections 376/377/313/323/ 506/509/120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 as well as subsequent chargesheet dated 20.09.2023, 07.12.2023 and 20.01.2025, and further seeks grant of interim stay on the proceedings arising out of the aforesaid FIR.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 12/08/2025 at 22:05:44 4.

Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the impugned FIR is nothing but a gross misuse of process of law, and the same has been lodged with mala fide intentions and an ulterior motive of vengeance against the petitioner.
5. Issue notice.
Learned APP for State, who appears on advance notice, accepts notice and seeks some time to file status report/reply.
Let the same be filed three days prior to the next date of hearing.

sentences.text:
In view of the mandate of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jagjeet Singh & Ors. vs. Ashish Mishra @
Monu & Anr., 2022 9 SCC 321, the complainant/victim is entitled to be heard in the present proceedings.

entities.text:
Jagjeet Singh & Ors. vs. Ashish Mishra @
Monu & Anr., 2022 9 SCC 321
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, let intimation be sent by the Investigating Officer to the complainant/victim informing them that they are entitled to be heard in the present proceedings,
for which they may remain present (either in-person or via video-conferencing) or be represented on the next date.
7. Let proof of service of intimation be placed on record before the next date.
8. List on 27.10.2025.
AJAY DIGPAUL, J AUGUST 8, 2025 gs/
